feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence so far: iterations 0 to 7 all used sensor y = 0.05 m, so sensor lead has never been tested and this is the first real test of it. In iteration 6 (mass 0.6 kg, track 0.10 m, body 0.10 m) the s-bend and slalom progress was 0.181 and 0.191, with max_error about 0.062 to 0.065 and the oval finish rate at 65%. In iteration 7 the mass was reduced to 0.5 kg with everything else unchanged. The s-bend progress fell to 0.140 and the slalom stayed flat at 0.186, so mass is not the limit on those tracks, and returning to lower mass is not a good next step. The Integrator has kept the controller fixed so this race isolates the lead change. Decide the next step from the race. If the s-bend and slalom progress rise above about 0.18 with max_error no worse than 0.062 m, keep y at 0.03 m. If the s-bend progress falls below 0.14 or max_error rises above 0.065 m, the shorter lead is too late for the bends, so return y to 0.05 m. If the oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25, restore mass to 0.6 kg while keeping y at 0.03 m.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress falls below 0.14 or max_error rises above 0.065 m at y 0.03 m, return every sensor y to 0.05 m and keep mass at 0.5 kg. Evidence: iteration 7 (mass 0.5 kg, y 0.05 m) gave s-bend progress 0.140, so a lead shorter than that may be worse on the bends.

If the oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25 with y 0.03 m, set mass back to 0.6 kg with x and the other geometry fixed. Evidence: iteration 6 oval oscillation was 0.216 at mass 0.6 kg and iteration 7 was 0.208 at mass 0.5 kg, both at y 0.05 m, so the oval is near the threshold and mass 0.6 kg is the known-stable setting.

If the s-bend and slalom progress are both above 0.18 with max_error at or below 0.062 m at y 0.03 m, keep the lead and try sensor_size 0.012 with the same x positions. Evidence: sensor_size 0.012 gave lower rms_error in iterations 1 and 2 (0.024 and 0.019), while 0.016 m gave 0.019 to 0.022 in iterations 3 to 7, so a smaller footprint is worth testing once the lead is settled.
